name: Japan
note: A doctor's death certificate is attached to the death notification (死亡届), which relatives must lodge with a municipal mayor within 7 days of learning of the death. Acceptance of the notice gates the burial/cremation permit and is entered in the family register (koseki). From there the death travels on its own: the resident record is deleted and pushed through J-LIS (住基ネット) to the Japan Pension Service, the electoral commission is told, vital statistics are generated, and the Ministry of Justice and mayor notify the tax authorities. Private bodies have no official feed and rely on koseki transcripts presented by heirs.

citations.title: Deadline and contents of the death notification
citations.quote: 死亡の届出は、届出義務者が、死亡の事実を知つた日から七日以内（国外で死亡があつたときは、その事実を知つた日から三箇月以内）に、これをしなければならない。

citations.title: Medical certificate must be attached
citations.quote: 届書には、次の事項を記載し、診断書又は検案書を添付しなければならない。

citations.title: Persons obliged to notify a death, in order
citations.quote: 次の者は、その順序に従つて、死亡の届出をしなければならない。ただし、順序にかかわらず届出をすることができる。

citations.title: Other persons who may notify

citations.title: Place of notification

citations.title: Notification at the place of death
citations.quote: 死亡の届出は、死亡地でこれをすることができる。

citations.title: Official report of deaths in disasters

citations.cite: 住民基本台帳法 (Basic Resident Registration Act), art. 15(2)

citations.cite: 人口動態調査令 (Vital Statistics Survey Order), arts. 2–3

citations.quote: 旅券は、次の各号のいずれかに該当する場合には、その効力を失う。旅券の名義人が死亡し、又は日本の国籍を失つたとき。

citations.quote: 相続は、死亡によって開始する。

citations.quote: 登記所の登記官に対し、法定相続情報…を記載した書面…の保管及び法定相続情報一覧図の写しの交付の申出をすることができる。

steps.title: Doctor examines the body and issues the death certificate
steps.localName: 死亡診断書・死体検案書
steps.who: The physician who attended (死亡診断書) or examined the body (死体検案書).
steps.summary: A doctor may only issue a certificate of death (死亡診断書) or post-mortem examination certificate (死体検案書) after personally examining; a doctor who examined must issue one on request. There is no nurse pronouncement route in the Act.

steps.title: Doctor reports an abnormal death to the police
steps.who: Any doctor who examines a body and finds it abnormal (異状).
steps.summary: A doctor who finds a body abnormal must report it to the local police station within 24 hours; the death then follows the medicolegal route rather than an ordinary certificate.

steps.title: Prosecutor (or police on delegation) conducts an inquest
steps.who: The public prosecutor of the district; may delegate to police officers.
steps.trigger: An unnatural death or suspected unnatural death.
steps.summary: Japan has no coroner: the public prosecutor must conduct an inquest (検視) of any unnatural or suspected unnatural death, usually delegated to judicial police officers.

steps.title: Notify the death to the municipal mayor (koseki registrar)
steps.who: In order: cohabiting relatives, other cohabitants, landlord/landowner/building manager; other relatives, guardians and appointed voluntary guardians may also notify.

deadline.text: within 7 days of learning of the death (3 months if abroad)

steps.summary: The death notification (死亡届) with the attached medical certificate is lodged with the mayor of the deceased's registered domicile, the notifier's location or the place of death. Failure without good reason is punishable by a civil fine of up to ¥50,000.

steps.title: Officials report disaster deaths and unidentified bodies
steps.who: The investigating authority for disaster deaths; police officers for unidentified bodies (with the inquest record).
steps.trigger: Death in a disaster, or a body whose domicile or identity is unknown.
steps.summary: Where a death occurs in a flood, fire or other disaster, the investigating authority reports it to the mayor; for unidentified bodies the police report with the inquest record, and relatives must notify within 10 days of identifying the deceased.

steps.title: Mayor who accepted the death notification issues the burial/cremation permit
steps.who: The mayor who accepted the death notification; the crematorium/cemetery manager receives the permit.
steps.summary: Burial or cremation needs a permit from the mayor who received the death notification, so registration gates disposal; no burial or cremation may take place within 24 hours of death, and a crematorium may not cremate without the permit.

steps.title: Death recorded in the koseki; copies on request
steps.who: The person recorded, spouse, lineal ascendants and descendants; others only for listed reasons (exercising rights, legal duties, legitimate interest); state bodies and listed professionals (lawyers, judicial scriveners, tax accountants) for their work.
steps.trigger: Entry of the death in the family register.
steps.summary: Japan issues no separate death certificate: the death is entered in the family register and evidenced by a koseki transcript (戸籍謄本・抄本 / 戸籍証明書). Access is restricted to the family and to third parties who state a qualifying reason.

steps.title: Image of the notification sent to the Minister of Justice
steps.who: The designated mayor (all municipalities on the networked koseki system).
steps.summary: The mayor creates image data of the death notification and sends it electronically to the Minister of Justice, who stores it; the koseki itself is kept on a networked electronic system linked to the Ministry.

steps.title: Resident record deleted and change pushed to J-LIS (住基ネット)
steps.localName: 住民票の消除・住基ネット
steps.who: The mayor (forwarding to the municipality of residence if different), then the prefectural governor, then J-LIS.
steps.summary: The resident record (住民票) is deleted on the basis of the koseki notification; where the deceased lived in another municipality the koseki office notifies it electronically. The deletion is then sent to the prefecture and on to J-LIS, which keeps the national Basic Resident Registration Network copy.

steps.title: Japan Pension Service learns of the death from 住基ネット
steps.localName: 住基ネットによる死亡確認
steps.who: J-LIS provides data to the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare and the Japan Pension Service on request for National Pension Act work.
steps.summary: The Japan Pension Service is a listed recipient of J-LIS identity data. For pensioners and insured persons whose data it can obtain this way, the separate pension death notice is waived if the koseki death notification was made within 7 days of death.

steps.title: Family files a pension death notice where not waived
steps.who: The persons obliged to notify the death under the Family Register Act.
steps.trigger: Death of a pensioner or insured person not covered by the 住基ネット waiver.
steps.summary: Where the waiver does not apply (e.g. no J-LIS data, or the koseki notice was late), the koseki notifiers must file a pension death notice (死亡届) with the Japan Pension Service or the municipality within 14 days.

steps.title: Mayor notifies the electoral commission; name struck off
steps.who: The mayor, to the municipal election administration commission.
steps.summary: When a resident record is changed the mayor must tell the municipal election commission, which must immediately delete a person from the electoral roll on learning of the death.

steps.title: Mayor prepares the vital statistics death form
steps.who: The mayor who received the notification, for the Minister of Health, Labour and Welfare.
steps.summary: Every death notification generates a vital statistics death form (死亡票) prepared by the mayor from the koseki documents.

steps.title: Ministry of Justice and mayor notify the tax authorities
steps.who: The Minister of Justice (to the NTA Commissioner) and the mayor (land and building tax-ledger data to the local tax office).
steps.trigger: Receipt of the death notification data.

deadline.text: by the end of the following month

steps.summary: On receiving the death-notice image data the Minister of Justice must pass the death to the National Tax Agency by the end of the following month; the mayor separately sends the deceased's fixed-asset tax ledger data to the tax office.

steps.title: Passport lapses automatically on death
steps.who: No notification step is set by the Act.
steps.summary: A passport ceases to be valid when its holder dies; the Act does not itself provide for a data feed to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

steps.title: Heirs obtain the certified statutory heir information list
steps.localName: 法定相続情報証明制度
steps.who: Heirs (or their agents) apply to a Legal Affairs Bureau registrar (登記官).
steps.trigger: Need to prove heirship for registration or other procedures.
steps.summary: Heirs may lodge a family-tree list with the Legal Affairs Bureau and receive certified copies (法定相続情報一覧図の写し) stating the deceased's date of death and the heirs. Banks and other bodies have no official death-data route; they rely on these documents or koseki transcripts presented by the family.

steps.title: Heirs must register inherited real property
steps.localName: 相続登記の申請義務化
steps.who: Heirs who acquired ownership of registered land/buildings, to the Legal Affairs Bureau.
steps.trigger: Knowledge of the succession and the acquisition.
steps.summary: Since 2024 inheritance registration of real property is compulsory within 3 years, on pain of a civil fine of up to ¥100,000.

steps.title: Heirs file an inheritance tax return
steps.who: Heirs and legatees whose taxable share exceeds the basic exemption.

deadline.text: within 10 months of learning of the succession

steps.summary: Where inheritance tax is due, the heirs file a return within ten months of learning that the succession opened.

steps.title: Heirs accept or renounce at the family court
steps.summary: An heir must accept (simply or with limited liability) or renounce within three months, extendable by the family court; there is no statutory public notice of the death itself.

registrationDeadlineDays.note: 7 days from learning of the death (3 months if the death occurred abroad).

informantDuty.note: Cohabiting relatives first, then other cohabitants, then the landlord or building manager; other relatives and guardians may notify.

medicalExaminerScrutiny.note: No independent review of ordinary certificates; abnormal deaths go to the police and prosecutor.

electronicRegistration.note: The informant lodges a paper notification at the municipal office; the koseki and onward transmission to the Ministry of Justice are electronic.

centralPopulationRegister.name: 住民基本台帳ネットワークシステム (Basic Resident Registration Network, J-LIS) over municipal koseki and 住民票
centralPopulationRegister.note: Municipal resident records feed J-LIS, which supplies listed national bodies.

governmentPropagation.note: One koseki notification updates the resident register, J-LIS, pensions (where the waiver applies), the electoral roll, vital statistics and the National Tax Agency.

certificateAccess.note: Koseki copies go to the registered persons, spouse and lineal relatives; others only with a stated qualifying reason or as listed professionals.

privateSectorVerification.note: No official route for banks or insurers to check deaths; they rely on koseki transcripts or the statutory heir information certificate the family presents.

gaps: No statutory duty or official data service for banks, insurers or credit bureaus to learn of deaths was found; private institutions rely on koseki transcripts and the 法定相続情報 certificate.
Whether driving licences (道路交通法) or health insurance (国民健康保険法 / 後期高齢者医療) records are updated automatically from the 住民票 deletion was not established from statute text.
Online (マイナポータル) submission of the 死亡届 was not found in the Family Register Act; electronicRegistration recorded as 'none' for the informant step.
The Ministry of Justice 'death certificate form' rules (死亡診断書記入マニュアル, MHLW) and 戸籍法施行規則 were not read; the medical-examiner (監察医) system under 死体解剖保存法 art. 8 in designated cities is not recorded.
Passport: the Act makes the passport lapse on death but no notification route to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs was found.
